title: The Bid
logline: At a harbour fish auction, hands rise and fall in seconds, and a trader must decide, before doubt catches up with them, whether this is the lot worth having.
human_question: What does it take, in a moment of real money and real doubt, to actually make up your mind?

premise.story: A fish auction at a working harbour, where traders bid fast on lots as they come off the boats, and doubt, decision and regret all show on the auction floor in public.
premise.place: A fishing harbour's wholesale auction floor at dawn.
premise.experience: The viewer feels the speed and pressure of the auction, and starts to notice the small, visible moment where hesitation turns into a raised hand, or doesn't.

concept_links.why: The source states that decision and doubt cannot occupy the same moment [C025-P:L69]. The auction floor is a place where the switch from doubt to decision is unusually visible and has real stakes.

The source's account of which of the thirteen ethically variable factors combine in which minds shows decision, effort and doubt as a shifting, neutral toolkit; the auction shows the same toolkit under real financial pressure.
The bare, rootless moment of seeing a lot of fish arrive, before any judgement of price or quality, is the sensing layer the source describes beneath every bid that follows.

what_camera_could_observe: Lots of fish tipped out or displayed
Traders' eyes and hands as bidding opens
A raised hand, a withdrawn bid, a hesitation
The auctioneer's call and the moment a lot is sold
Traders afterward, discussing what they got and what they missed
what_must_be_real: The traders' real money and livelihoods; no staged bids or manufactured drama. The economics of fishing families behind the auction must not be reduced to metaphor.

possible_arc.opening: Boats come in; the day's lots are laid out.
possible_arc.turn: A difficult lot, uncertain quality, a rival bidder, a tight budget, forces a real decision.
possible_arc.ending_open: The morning's trading ends as it actually does, with winners and losers on both sides.

position_hint: middle: a fast, public, high-stakes setting that contrasts with the group's quieter craft-based films.

requirements: An active wholesale fish auction at a working harbour
Trader and auctioneer consent to filming real transactions
Safe camera positions amid fast-moving, wet, crowded conditions

suggestions.name: Negombo Fisheries Harbour (Lellama)
suggestions.why: A major, well-known fishing harbour with an active wholesale auction.
suggestions.access_notes: Early-morning access and harbour authority permission would be needed.
suggestions.verify: Specific auction schedules and trader consent are unverified.

risks: Portraying traders as simply greedy rather than as people managing real risk
The economics of fishing families should not be reduced to a metaphor for a mental-factor lesson
Fast, crowded, wet conditions carry real safety and equipment risks
drop_if: No harbour or auction allows filming of real trading
Traders do not want their bidding and losses shown on camera
The auction turns out to be too small or irregular to sustain a film

connections.note: A public decision made under pressure and doubt leads naturally into the group's closing film about a harder, more consequential decision.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
